summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with chest pain and hyperkalemia. Initial evaluation revealed fluid overload and elevated potassium, managed with medical therapy and dialysis. Her left arm arteriovenous fistula, previously complicated by steal syndrome, was evaluated with a fistulogram, which revealed stenosis. During attempted angioplasty, the fistula ruptured, causing a hematoma that required surgical evacuation. The fistula was rendered nonfunctional, and a temporary right subclavian dialysis line was placed, later converted to a tunneled catheter. Her chest pain resolved, potassium normalized, and INR stabilized after warfarin adjustment. She was discharged home with instructions to protect her right arm for future fistula creation, continue medications, monitor weight, and follow up with transplant surgery and nephrology.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
Kidney dialysis as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
